To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the region of NCX1 at the interface of transmembrane segment two and cytoplasmic loops b is important in Na+/Ca2+-transport and secondary regulation.

the region of NCX1 that connects transmembrane segment one to two is on the cytoplsmic side of the plasma membrane and mutations at residues in that region alter the transport properties of the exchanger.

a mutation in a region at the interface between transmembrane segments two and loop b, aspartate 101 to cystein, renders the exchanger unresponsive to Na+ and Li+ and insensitive to regulation by Ca2+, whereas a nearby mutation in the same loop, threonine 102 to cystein, increases Li+ and Na+ transport and increases the apparent affinity of NCX1 for Na+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topology of the cardiac Na+/Ca+2 exchanger.
the molecular structure-function of the cardiac Na+/Ca++ exchanger.
the topology of a functionally important region of the cardiac Na+/Ca++ exchanger.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has provided evidence that the region at or near the interface of transmembrane segment two and cytoplasmic domain b is important in the function of the cardiac Na+/Ca+ exchanger.
this region of the exchanger may be involved in the regulation of Na+ transport.

the region of the exchanger that is important to the regulation of the Na+/Ca2+-exchange reaction has been identified and is located in the cytoplasm at the interface between transmembrane segments TM2 and loop b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the region at loop b-transmembrane 2 interface has a role in the regulation of the Na+ binding site and that this region is in close proximity to the Ca2+ binding site.
the topology of NCX1 is consistent with the previously published model.
the region at or near the interface of loop b and transmemebrane 2 is important for ion transport and regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the topology of the cardiac Na+/Ca+ exchanger is not as simple as the original model proposed by Philipps et al. (1989), but that the exchanger has an additional loop between the transmembrane helices 1 and 3.
the region between transmembrane segments two and three is functionally important and is located on the inside of the cell.

NCX1 is a complex and highly regulated ion transporter, and the regulation is likely to be a result of the interplay between the transmembrane domains and the cytoplasmically located regulatory sites.
